title: Dynamic chunking and prefix-cache TTL tradeoff sweep
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We need a controlled, reproducible sweep to quantify the latency vs. quality tradeoffs when applying two common runtime knobs simultaneously: dynamic chunking (microbatch granularity and chunk threshold heuristics) and prefix-cache TTL (how long cached KV/prefix entries are considered hot).

Problem: Past changes that tightened batching heuristics or shortened cache TTLs reduced tail latency but introduced subtle quality regressions for long-context prompts (observed as token-level perplexity increases and confusion in multi-step instructions). Existing evaluations focus on single-dimension sensitivity (batch size OR TTL) but not their interaction. This ticket scopes an experiments matrix and rollout gating rules to safely surface practical operating points.

Hypothesis: Moderate increases in chunking granularity (smaller microbatches with adaptive coalescing) plus a short prefix-TTL (e.g., 30s) will reduce 95th/99th percentile latency by ~12-25% for bursty workloads with <2s generation windows while maintaining aggregate quality within a 0.8% cross-entropy delta and <2% regression on metric-based evals. Extreme reductions in TTL or aggressive microbatching will harm long-sequence coherence and instruction-following.

Why now: We plan a rollout of runtime-1.22 which includes a new batched coalescer and an LRU refresh for prefix cache. We must validate default config recommendations and add monitoring/rollback hooks to Console rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Define a 3x3 sweep grid across chunking mode {static-16, adaptive-32, micro-8} and prefix-TTL {15s, 60s, 300s}
Run automated evals on representative production prompt set (10k prompts across short, medium, long) with deterministic seed and record latency distributions and quality metrics
Establish safe-default config(s) with documented unit economics (tokens/sec, %cost delta) and quality delta thresholds
Add two console alerts: (1) token-level perplexity drift >1% and (2) instruction-following failure rate >2% during rollout; both must auto-trigger canary rollback
Publish a concise PRD with rollout playbook, experimental data, and recommended runtime-1.22 defaults
experiment_plan: Dataset: 10k de-identified production prompts sampled by length buckets (0-128, 129-1024, >1024 tokens) + canonical synthetic stress cases (long chained instructions, stateful multi-turn)
Matrix: chunking_mode x prefix_TTL x two traffic patterns (steady vs bursty) = 18 experiments

Measurements per experiment: 1000 warm requests + 5k steady-state requests; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, end-to-end generation time, cross-entropy delta, token-level perplexity, and an instruction-following binary metric from heuristic parser
Quality eval: automated BLEU/ROUGE-like signals for retrieval-style prompts plus a 200-sample human review for long-context coherence for top-3 candidate configs
Infrastructure: run experiments on dedicated infra pool (dedicated-evals-4xA100) to avoid noisy neighbors; use config sweeper service to spin variants and collect traces to S3
Comparisons: baseline = current runtime-1.21 defaults; also include a conservative fallback (static-32, TTL 300s)
Duration: each sweep run expected to finish in 6-8 hours; plan two full passes (dry-run + high-confidence run)
Rollout gating: auto-promote if p95 latency improvement >=10% AND cross-entropy delta <=0.8% AND human-fail-rate delta <=1%
metrics: Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec under steady-state
Quality: token-level cross-entropy delta vs baseline (ppm), perplexity, instruction-following pass-rate (heuristic)
Cost proxy: GPU-token-seconds and estimated $/1M tokens
Stability: cache hit-rate, cache eviction rate, cache refresh churn, microbatch coalescer wait time distribution
User-visible: human-rated coherence score (1-5) on long-context samples
